art-and-culture.name: Haveli Barood Khana
art-and-culture.description: Built in the 18th century by a Sikh commanding general and used as a house. Considering the hot temperature of Lahore, the haveli has high ceilings. The room also has murals of the Sikh general fighting demons.

art-and-culture.name: National Museum of Pakistan
art-and-culture.description: The National Museum of Pakistan established in Frere Hall on 17 April 1950. In 1950 with a primary duty to counsel the Museum on the issues of enriching its collection through new acquisitions and purchase of antiquities and works of Arts. The Museum was shifted in Burns Garden in 1970.

art-and-culture.name: Khaliq Dina Hall
art-and-culture.description: Khaliq Dina Hall is a library and hall located in Karachi, Pakistan built in 1906. Currently used for various events, a library, and a room that serves as the office of a local NGO.

art-and-culture.name: Haveli of Nau Nihal Singh
art-and-culture.description: The haveli is considered to be one of the finest examples of Sikh architecture in Lahore preserved in its original architecture.

art-and-culture.name: Nigar Khana
art-and-culture.description: Nigar Khana known as a House of Art for selling handicrafts, exhibits antiquities, cultural and artistic items for over 45 years. one finds oneself into a world of colors consisted of mosaic art, Naqashi, wooden, glass work etc.

art-and-culture.name: Sethi street
art-and-culture.description: Made in the nineteenth century Finely assembled 05 places of Sethi family are situated here close by other houses.

explore-cities.name: NagarParkar
explore-cities.description: Nagarparkar, near the PakistanâIndia border, lies at the foot of the Karoonjhar Hills and is known for its desert scenery, granite outcrops, and rich cultural heritage. Home to ancient Jain temples, Hindu shrines, and the historic Bhodesar Mosque, it offers a unique blend of history, spirituality, and Thari cultureâespecially vibrant during the monsoon season.

explore-cities.name: hyderabad
explore-cities.description: Hyderabad, the Lion's City, with its historical architecture, rich history, and scrumptious Sindhi cuisine is one of the best go-to cities in Sindh.

explore-cities.name: Skardu
explore-cities.description: touristâs paradise offering lush, level meadows in the form of the Deosai Plains, a dreamy lakeside resort and high-altitude desert with both sand dunes and snow.

explore-cities.name: Kasur
explore-cities.description: Kasur also Romanized as QasÅ«r is a city to south of Lahore, in the Pakistani province of Punjab. It is also known for being the burial place of the 17th-century Sufi-poet Bulleh Shah. Kasur derives its name from the Arabic word qasur meaning âpalaces,â or âfortsâ.

explore-cities.name: Quetta
explore-cities.description: The city is known as the "Fruit Garden of Pakistan," due to the numerous fruit orchards in and around it, and the large variety of fruits and dried fruit products produced there.

explore-cities.name: Karachi: The City of lights
explore-cities.description: Karachi is the largest city of Pakistan. With its dazzling bazaars, high-end shopping malls, amazing sightseeing options, and a mix of all cultures, it is surely a must-visit.

explore-cities.name: Lahore
explore-cities.description: A city where history, culture, and hospitality come alive. Explore its grand Mughal monuments, vibrant bazaars, rich cuisine, and lively streets that never sleep.

traditional-food.name: Pindi Food Street
traditional-food.description: A must visit place for the food lovers, if one is visiting Rawalpindi. There are a variety of restaurants and food to enjoy with family and friends.

traditional-food.name: Do Darya
traditional-food.description: With a great atmosphere, multiple cuisine options, and beautiful views, restaurants at Do Darya have quickly garnered a reputation and a loyal customers from all over the city. Nothing can top the experience of the Do Darya food scene.

traditional-food.name: Lahore Fort Food Street
traditional-food.description: Travelers from all across the world come to feast on some of the most delicious desi food. Offering enchanting views of Badshahi Mosque and Lahore Fort, the delicious food is bound to make your visit to this food street unforgettable.

traditional-food.name: Sindhi Muslim Food St
traditional-food.description: A popular spot for all the foodies out there, from BBQ to mouth watering burgers. This food street will make anyone want to visit it over and over again.

spiritual-tourism.name: Bhodesar Mosque
spiritual-tourism.description: This mosque with white pillars in Bhodesar is a small marble and limestone structure near the pond embankment is built in 1436 AD. It was built by Mehmood Shah Bin Zaffar Shah, ruler of Gujrat. The mosque is located 5 Km from town Nagarparkar.

spiritual-tourism.name: Mirza Jani Baig Tarkhan's Tomb
spiritual-tourism.description: The mausoleum of Mirza Jani Baig Tarkhan presents a picturesque and colourful sight. The brick masonry, in alternate courses of glazed dark-blue and unglazed red bricks, represents a high standard of Sindhi craftsmanship.

spiritual-tourism.name: Lahoot Lamakan
spiritual-tourism.description: Lahoot Lamakan is a cave in Balochistan, Pakistan. The water flows from the external limestone shell of the cave and believers have a tale that first it was milk when people began to sell it, miraculously it became water.

spiritual-tourism.name: Sharada Peeth
spiritual-tourism.description: Sharada Peeth is a ruined Hindu temple and ancient centre of learning between 6th and 12th century CE. It played a key role in the development and popularisation of the Sharada script in North India, causing the script to be named after it.

spiritual-tourism.name: Badshahi Mosque
spiritual-tourism.description: The Badshahi Mosque of Lahore was constructed by the Mughal emperor Aurangzeb between 1671 and 1673 and was the largest mosque in the world from 1673 to 1986.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Changa Manga Forest
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: The Changa Manga is a planted forest which includes a wildlife preserve, in the Kasur and Lahore districts of Punjab. The Changa Manga forest was originally planted in 1866 by British foresters. The forest is home to many species of animals.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Fort Munroe Hill
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Fort Munro named after a British administrator, Col Munroe is located in Southern Punjab at the foothills of the Suleiman Range. It attracts a number of tourists every year, particularly those who wish to escape from the hot plains of southern Punjab.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Dreamworld Resort
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: At Dreamworld Resort, you along with your family will be able to keep yourself entertained throughout the stay. Providing a serene and tranquil gateway of quality living for the whole family and to rejuvenate ones mind and body.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Attabad Lake
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Attabad Lake is in Gojal region of Hunza -a mountainous valley in the northern part of the Gilgit-Baltistan formed by the Hunza River, bordering Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor to the north and the Xinjiang region of China to the northeast.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Mubarak Village Beach
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: The crystal clear greenish-blue waters and unspoiled coastline have made this spot gain immense popularity in recent years. One can indulge in all sorts of water sports on the trip to Mubarak Village, including boating, beaching, snorkeling, and scuba diving.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Khunjerab
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: A gateway between two great allies , the incredible altitude makes for a very memorable, albeit chilly, experience, which has captured the imaginations of the local people.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: K2
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: The legendary K2 is the second highest mountain in the world. It is located in the north-western Karakoram Mountain Range on the PakistanâChina border

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Passu Cones
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Breathtaking views of majestic Passu Cones (few pointed cone-like snow covered peaks) are in the Karakorum Range in north of the Gulmit village in Gojal Valley.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Rakaposhi
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Part of the Karakoram range, Rakaposhi is the 27th highest mountain in the world. The mountain resides in the middle of the Bagrote valley, danyor and Nagar Valley.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Kallar Kahar
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Alluring scenic beauty, with a calm lake, and breathtaking views, where you can go for cliff-diving, paragliding and many more activities.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Soon Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Soon Valley is a breathtaking vista of natural beauty consisting of lakes and springs, lush green fertile fields. Accessible through Kallar Kahar, Soon Valley extends to almost 100 kilometers.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Neela Sandh Waterfall
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Neela Sandh is a delightful waterfall, situated in Mori Syedan, Rawalpindi, Punjab. It has numerous greenery, tall trees and extensive mountains which are relatively secured with snow constantly. Guests who adore swimming unquestionably visit to enjoy with their families and companions.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Shandur Lake
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Shandur Lake is located on a high mountain pass, âShandur Passâ. It is also called the âRoof of the Worldâ and is one of the most beautiful lakes of Pakistan. The spot is most well known in view of the Shandur Polo Festival.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Kai Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Kai Valley presents a picturesque panorama on both sides of the road. Kai Valley is one of the rare solitary landscapes which sees the majority of tourists. It gives the impression as if the hills were once underneath sea.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Shandur Pass
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Known as the 'Roof of the World' where the Hindu Kush, Pamir Mountains and Karakorum Range meet, Shandur is located in the Upper Chitral District of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, Pakistan and is location of annual Shandur Polo Festival.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Karimabad
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Karimabad, previously known as Baltit, is named after Prince Karim Aga Khan IV. It is the capital of Hunza District, in the Gilgit-Baltistan area of Pakistan.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Masherbrum
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Masherbrum, formerly known as K1 is located in the Ghanche District, Gilgit Baltistan. At 25,659 feet, it is the 22nd highest mountain in the world.  The mighty Masherbrum Peaks in Pakistan are perfect for every tough mountaineer to prepare themselves for higher altitude peaks.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Swaik Lake
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Swaik Lake also known as âKhandowa Lakeâ is located in tehsil Kallar Kahar, Punjab. Itâs crystal clear water and serene atmosphere offers adventure lovers just the right mix of thrill with ease of access. It is a popular tourist attraction and offers opportunities for swimming and diving.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Khunjerab National Park
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Khunjerab National Park is Pakistan's third largest national park. The park is adjacent to the Taxkorgan Natural Reserve in China. The primary purpose of setting up this park was to provide protection to the endangered Marco polo sheep, which is only found in this area in Pakistan.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Nathia Gali
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Ideal for hiking, trekking and sightseeing, with its crowning jewel, Mushkpuri peak, Nathia Gali is the place to experience nature's true beauty.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Khaplu Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Khaplu is a city that serves as the managerial capital of the Ghanche District of Gilgit-Baltistan, in northern Pakistan.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Karambar Lake
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Karambar Lake, renowned as Qurumbar Lake, is a high height lake situated in the Ishkoman Valley bilanz in Ghizer District, Gilgit Baltistan, Pakistan.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Naltar Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: renowned for its lakes whose waters change colours depending on the time of day. The three lakes are known by several names. According to locals, one of the lakes is called the Pari Lake because of its enchanting, deep blue colour.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Phander Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Phander is the name of a settlement and valley in the Gupis-Yasin District of Pakistan's reliant region of Gilgit-Baltistan.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Karakoram Mountains
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: The Karakoram is a mountain range spanning the borders of China, India, and Pakistan. The mountain range is a great challenge for the mountaineers & climbers the world over.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Kund Malir Beach
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Kund Malir beach with its sparkling cerulean waters, beckons visitors to spend the day picnicking or the night camping on its peaceful shore. Add a to that bonfire as the Milky Way unfolds above and it makes for the perfect weekend getaway.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Hushe Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Hushe Valley is a valley in Ghanche District, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan. Created by the Hushe River, the valley runs from Masherbrum Mountain (at 7,821 meters) and close by glaciers south to the Shyok River, inverse Khaplu.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Hingol National Park,Balochistan
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Hingol National Park is the largest national park in Pakistan and is named after the southern part of the Hangul River which flows along the shores of the Arabian Sea and is home to large numbers of waterfowl and marine life.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Baha Lake
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Baha Lake is also known as Khukush Langar Lake is a colossal lake lying at the feet of transcending mountains.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Katpana Desert
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Katpana desert is one of its kind. Being one of the highest deserts, its temperature varies from 27 Â°C in summers to snow covered sand in winters.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Shogran Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Shogran, one of the most beautiful plateaus in Naran Valley.  From the rolling grassy lawns of the rest house, one can see breathtaking panoramic views of snow covered mountains.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Ishkoman
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: The Ishkoman valley lies in the north of Ghizer District in Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan, lining Afghanistan and the Pamir Wakhan Corridor.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Jiwani Coastal Wetland
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Jiwani is a town and commercial port that is located along the Gulf of Oman in the Gawadar District of the Balochistan province in Pakistan.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Bagrote
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Bagrote Valley is a valley in the Karakoram Mountain range in the GilgitâBaltistan district of northern Pakistan.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Nagar
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: In an eponymous valley with splendid scenery, Nagar is a small town. A visit during the right season, you can see trees of many different colors with lakes, rivers, and clear skies abound.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Diran peak
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Standing at the height of 7,266 Meters, Diran is a sight to behold. This pyramid shaped mountain is known as the most dangerous mountain of Pakistan due to large snow caps.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Cholistan
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: The Cholistan Desert, locally known as Rohi, stretches across southern Punjab, Pakistan, extending into Sindh and the Indian Thar Desert. Covering over 26,000â¯kmÂ², it was once a fertile plain nourished by the ancient Hakra (Ghaggar) River. Today it's home to more than 400 Indus Valley Civilization archaeological sites

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Leepa Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Leepa Valley is located in Hattian Bala District of Azad Kashmir. With fields of rice apple found all over the valley, its lush green river fields in summer and typical wooden kashmiri houses present a wonderful view to the tourists.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Zharba Tso/Blind lake
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Zharba Tso or Blind lake is a Panoramic Lake close to Shigar around 170 km away from Skardu in Pakistan.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Wali Tangi Dam Lake
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Wali Tangi Dam is a little dam in the Urak Valley in Balochistan territory of Pakistan. It is arranged around 20 km east of Quetta at a rise of roughly 8,350 ft.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Neelum Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: The valley is situated in the northeast of Muzaffarabad, running parallel to Kaghan Valley. It is replete with gorgeous scenery, stunning valleys, and magical waterfalls.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Hunza Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Hunza is a mountainous valley in the northern part of the Gilgit-Baltistan formed by the Hunza River, bordering Afghanistan's Wakhan Corridor to the north and the Xinjiang region of China to the northeast.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Bhit Khori
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Bhit Khori, one of the finest beaches in Pakistan, asks you to complete a rocky journey before it gifts you with its golden sands and beautiful, cerulean seawater.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Keenjhar Lake Resort
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: The resort is developed on the bank of Keenjhar lake, which is a favorable and ideal place for winter migratory birds that come from regions of North Asia in the winter season. Located in the center of Thatta district, which has important tourist sites belonging to the near and far past of history.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Fairy Meadows
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Named by some German climbers and locally known as Jaugth, Fairy Meadows is a grassland near one of Nanga Parbat's base campsites.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Gorakh Hill
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Gorakh Hill is a hill station of Sindh.  It is situated on one of the highest plateaus of Sindh, spread over 2,500 acres. The hill station is well known for itâs nightlife, especially for itâs bonfires.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Urak Valley
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Urak Valley is a valley encircled by mountains inside the Quetta Area of Balochistan Region, in western Pakistan. Urak Valley is found close to Hana Lake and 28 kilometers (17 mi) from Quetta city.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Khalti Lake
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Khalti Lake is located at Gupis-Yasin District, the westernmost piece of the GilgitâBaltistan locale and northernmost domain of Pakistan.

adventure-and-eco-tourism.name: Rush Lake
adventure-and-eco-tourism.description: Rush Lake is a high-altitude lake situated in Nagar Valley, Gilgit-Baltistan, Pakistan close to Rush Pari Peak. At 4,694 meters (15,400 ft), Rush is one of the most elevated high lakes on the planet.

cultural-tourism.name: Ganda Singh Wala
cultural-tourism.description: Ganda Singh Wala is a village in Kasur, Punjab. A daily 6 p.m Beating Retreat Border Ceremony is jointly held at the border crossing by the military of both nations. The ceremony is attended mostly by local Punjabi's on either side of the border.
